14-158.r: Space shuttle 'Discovery' (launched July 4, 2006) → fuel tanks held a mixture of liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen.

14-159.r: Apollo-8 → first mission to take humans to the Moon and back; launched 21 December 1968 from Cape Kennedy. All options (1998) wrong; the book gives no single answer (*).

14-160.r: Selene-1 → Japan's lunar orbiter, launched 14 September 2007; its nickname 'Kaguya' was chosen by the public.

14-161.r: Jet engine → takes oxygen from surrounding air, so unsuitable in space; rocket carries its own oxidiser and fuel as liquid or solid, not gas → only 1.

14-162.r: Jets fly smoothly in lower stratosphere → no clouds or water vapour and no vertical winds; no convection turbulence → both correct.

14-163.r: Jet engine (and rocket) → works on the principle of conservation of linear momentum.

14-164.r: Rocket → works on conservation of momentum: material ejected backward gives forward thrust; momentum p = mv.

14-165.r: Stratellite → high-altitude airship stationed in the stratosphere, carrying repeaters for wireless networks; like a satellite but not in orbit.

14-166.r: Cryogenic temperatures → below about –150°C (the cryogenic region is often taken as below about –153°C).

14-167.r: Cryogenics (low temperature) applications → space travel, magnetic levitation and telemetry.

14-168.r: Cryogenic engine → rocket technology: uses cryogenic fuel and oxidizer, gases liquefied and stored below –150°C; Greek 'Kryos' = frost.

14-169.r: Cryogenic engine → liquid oxygen as oxidizer and liquid hydrogen as fuel, stored at extremely low temperature; used in space shuttles.

14-171.r: Liquid hydrogen, liquid hydrazine, kerosene (fuels) and liquid oxygen (oxidiser) → all are rocket propellants. The book gives no single answer (*).

14-172.r: BEL (Bharat Electronics Ltd.) with ISRO → developing GaAs (Gallium Arsenide) space solar cells to lengthen Indian satellites' life.

14-173.r: India tested a full cryogenic stage (50 seconds, Mahendragiri, October 2006) → sixth in the club with USA, Russia, ESA, China, Japan; so statement 2 wrong.

14-174.r: PSLV-C12 (20 April 2009, Sriharikota) → orbited RISAT-2 (radar surveillance satellite for border watch) and ANUSAT (Anna University's experimental communication satellite) → all four correct.

14-175.r: Correct: PSLVs launch IRS satellites; GSLV's third stage used an indigenous cryogenic engine; GSAT-1 (18 April 2001) demonstrated digital broadcast and internet. Wrong: all INSATs launched abroad.

14-176.r: PSLV → Earth resources monitoring satellites; GSLV → mainly communication satellites. PSLV satellites do not stay fixed in the sky; Mk III stage description wrong → only 1.

14-177.r: Artificial satellite tracked very precisely from Earth → using the Doppler effect (with a tracking transmitter).

14-178.r: SLV-3 → a launch vehicle, not a satellite; RS-D1 (Rohini, 31 May 1981), IRS-1D (29 September 1997), INSAT-2D (4 June 1997) are satellites.

14-179.r: GSLV-D2 → a launch vehicle (second developmental flight, 8 May 2003), not a satellite; it placed the 1800 kg GSAT-2 in orbit. The book gives no single answer (*).

14-180.r: Vigyan Rail → Railways + Vigyan Prasar (not CSIR); Vigyan Prasar → under DST (not HRD); EDUSAT (20 September 2004) not launched from French Guiana → none correct.

14-182.r: METSAT (12 September 2002) → India's first full meteorological satellite, renamed Kalpana-I after Kalpana Chawla; PSLV-C4 first carried over 1000 kg (1060 kg) to geosynchronous orbit.

14-185.r: SATHYABAMASAT → academic institute micro satellite by Sathyabama University, Chennai, for greenhouse gas data; launched with Cartosat-2C on PSLV-C34, 22 June 2016.

14-186.r: GSAT-8 (advanced communication satellite) → launched 21 May 2011 by Ariane-V from Kourou, French Guiana.

14-187.r: GSAT-7 ('Rukmini', also INSAT-4F) → multi-band communication satellite dedicated to the Indian Navy (military); launched 30 August 2013 by Ariane-5 from Kourou.

14-188.r: Failed to reach orbit → GSAT-4 (April 2010, rocket's third stage malfunctioned) and GSAT-5P (25 December 2010).

14-189.r: 29 September 2012 → India launched telecommunication satellite GSAT-10 by Ariane-5 from Guiana Space Centre.

14-190.r: GSAT-6A (high-power S-band communication satellite) → launched by GSLV-F08 on 29 March 2018 from Sriharikota; mission life 10 years.

14-191.r: Bhuvan → ISRO's geoportal with 2D/3D imaging of Earth's surface; also gives disaster support; Indian version of Google Earth.

15-001.r: DRDO motto → 'Balasya Mulam Vigyanam'; DRDO formed in 1958 under Ministry of Defence; headquarters Delhi.
hi: Defence Research and Development Organisation (रक्षा अनुसंधान एवं विकास संगठन)

15-002.r: Indian Army's Quantum Computing Laboratory (2021) → Military College of Telecommunication Engineering, Mhow, Madhya Pradesh; set up with help of NSCS.

15-003.r: Mission Divyastra → first flight test of Agni-V with MIRV (Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicle) technology; DRDO, Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island, Odisha, 11 March 2024.

15-004.r: VSHORADS (Very Short-Range Air Defence System) → DRDO's 4th-generation man-portable air defence system (MANPADS), developed by Research Centre Imarat, Hyderabad.

15-005.r: Akashteer → core command-and-control of the Army's air defence; integrates with India's C4ISR network; shift from passive defence to proactive retaliation → more than one true.

15-006.r: Make in India indigenous platforms → MBT Arjun and ATAGS ('Amogh'); F-35 Lightning II is a U.S. stealth fighter → more than one of the above.

15-007.r: India's first indigenous anti-radiation missile → RudraM-I (NGARM), tested 9 October 2020 from Su-30 MKI at Wheeler Island, Odisha; range up to 200 km.

15-008.r: RudraM-II → DRDO's air-to-surface (not air-to-air) anti-radiation missile; tested from Su-30 MKI off Odisha (not Rajasthan) on 29 May 2024 → neither correct.

15-009.r: Nag → India's 'Fire and Forget' anti-tank missile; land version range 500 m to 4 km; first successful test 24 November 1990.

15-010.r: Prithvi → surface-to-surface missile; Trishul → surface-to-air missile; Pinaka → multi-barrel rocket launcher (not a missile); Nishant → remote-operated battlefield inspection vehicle.

15-012.r: Trishul → India's short-range surface-to-air missile (Integrated Guided Missile Development program); Prithvi and Agni → surface-to-surface; Nag → anti-tank.

15-014.r: Prithvi → India's surface-to-surface missile; Akash → medium-range mobile surface-to-air missile system.
15-014.h: Prithvi = earth → surface-to-surface; Akash = sky → surface-to-air.

15-015.r: Trishul → short-range surface-to-air; Prithvi → surface-to-surface; Agni → intermediate range ballistic system; NAG → anti-tank missile.

15-016.r: Akash → surface-to-air missile; Bahujan Samaj Party → Kanshiram (founder); Prithvi → surface-to-surface missile; Mirage 2000 → French fighter plane.
